html:
The Hola massacre took place on 3 March 1959 at the Hola detention camp in eastern Kenya, where guards beat eleven Mau Mau detainees to death for refusing to work.

The authorities first said the men had died from drinking bad water, but post-mortems showed they had been beaten. The news caused an outcry in Britain, and in Parliament Enoch Powell condemned the killings in a famous speech.

The scandal, with others in the colonies that year, convinced the British government to speed decolonisation. The emergency declared against the Mau Mau ended in 1960, and talks on majority rule began, leading to independence under Kenyatta in Kenya.
sum: The Hola massacre took place on 3 March 1959 at the Hola detention camp in eastern Kenya, where guards beat eleven Mau Mau detainees to death for refusing to work.
